nodes.label: Trip accommodations association
nodes.rationale: A separate association table models the many-to-many relationship and is owned by Student 1; Student 2 accesses it only through four public endpoints.

nodes.label: Idempotent accommodation pin
nodes.rationale: PUT is used because repeating a pin action must not conflict, and the trip start date is the only default date guaranteed to be inside the trip window.

nodes.label: Bounded accommodation identifier
nodes.rationale: The accommodation service owns identifier generation, so Student 1 validates a bounded portable character set rather than coupling to UUIDs.

nodes.label: Last-write-wins concurrency
nodes.rationale: PATCH uses read-merge-write because the internal API has no record versions or conditional writes; the database API remains the final validation guard.

nodes.label: Deferred live AI suggestions
nodes.rationale: Issue #11 exposes only a disabled AI affordance while live suggestions remain deferred to issue #12.

nodes.label: Disabled AI Suggestion Affordance
nodes.rationale: The suggestion controls are intentionally disabled until issue #12 wires live backend AI behavior, so the UI does not imply functionality that does not yet exist.

nodes.label: Contract-Ready AI Placeholder
nodes.rationale: CRUD remains live while AI suggestions stay disabled until the dedicated backend integration is implemented.

nodes.label: Independently Deployable Public Contract
nodes.rationale: The backend declares its own accommodation message so external callers depend on the public service rather than importing the internal database package, preserving independent deployment.

nodes.label: Whole Picker State Response
nodes.rationale: Every itinerary endpoint returns the complete picker state so one response can repaint the UI and its ticks cannot disagree with the state stored by Student 1.

nodes.label: Seed-on-Empty Database
nodes.rationale: A fresh database is seeded so the frontend list, filters, and pager have data to display; an existing non-empty database is left unchanged.

nodes.label: Omitted Field Semantics
nodes.rationale: Absent JSON fields mean not supplied rather than empty, preserving meaningful explicit values such as 0.0 and empty lists.

nodes.label: Stable Pagination Order
nodes.rationale: Results are ordered by name and then id so limit/offset pages cannot unpredictably repeat rows.

nodes.label: HTML-to-JSON Adapter Service
nodes.rationale: A separate frontend service is needed because HTMX consumes HTML fragments while the backend returns JSON, and because the QUERY request body cannot be issued directly by HTMX.

nodes.label: Automatic Pagination Reset
nodes.rationale: Offset exists only on pager controls, so changing any filter naturally returns the user to the first page.

nodes.label: Native Dialog Modal
nodes.rationale: The browser's native dialog supplies focus handling, Escape behavior, and backdrop rendering without a modal library.

nodes.label: Model-Owned Message Mapping
nodes.rationale: Rows translate themselves to and from wire messages, keeping routers small and avoiding a separate mapping layer.

nodes.label: Composition Over Accommodation Subclasses
nodes.rationale: Room and location details are composed values so one concrete Accommodation class remains queryable without isinstance branching.

nodes.label: Create-All During Schema Churn
nodes.rationale: Alembic is deferred while the schema is still moving; create_all is considered sufficient until migration pressure becomes real.

nodes.label: Backend-Authoritative Toggle
nodes.rationale: Every toggle replaces the full fragment from the backend response, preventing the visual checked state from diverging from stored state.

nodes.label: Native Destructive Confirmation
nodes.rationale: HTMX confirmation uses the browser's accessible native confirmation for the destructive removal half of the toggle.

nodes.label: Lazy Itinerary Picker
nodes.rationale: The itinerary list is fetched only when the disclosure first opens because most modal opens only inspect accommodation facts.

nodes.label: Incremental Graph Rebuild Hooks
nodes.rationale: Post-commit and post-checkout hooks refresh code relationships automatically, while documentation and images require explicit semantic extraction.

nodes.label: Duration-Bounded Valid Start Range
nodes.rationale: Valid starts run from start_time through end_time minus Activity.duration_minutes; an interval equal to duration behaves as a fixed session.

nodes.label: No Separate Schedule-Kind Field
nodes.rationale: The model derives fixed versus flexible behavior from interval length and activity duration, deliberately omitting a schedule-kind discriminator.

nodes.label: Tri-State Accessibility Facts
nodes.rationale: Nullable booleans distinguish confirmed absence from unknown status, and accessibility filters match only true values.

nodes.label: Local-Time Schedule
nodes.rationale: Dates and times remain local to the activity address until a future location service supplies timezone-aware conversion.

nodes.label: Student 4 Database Service
nodes.rationale: The database service is the sole owner of the tables and SQLite database.

nodes.label: Database Service Validation
nodes.rationale: Rules SQLite cannot express cleanly, especially interval-to-parent-duration comparisons, are enforced before transaction commit.

nodes.label: Independent Wire Schemas
nodes.rationale: Database and backend services declare separate schemas to preserve an independently deployable service boundary.
